facts.text: Son Bunyola is on Mallorca's north-west coast in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Tramuntana Mountains.
facts.excerpt: located on the island’s stunning north-west coast in the spectacular UNESCO World Heritage-listed Tramuntana Mountains

facts.text: The estate has three miles of unspoilt coastline, with olive groves and vineyards.
facts.excerpt: With three miles of unspoilt coastline, rugged shores, olive groves, vineyards and the untouched beauty of the Tramuntana mountain range

facts.text: The estate includes three standalone villas: Sa Punta de S'Aguila, Sa Terra Rotja and Son Balagueret.
facts.excerpt: three standalone luxury villas - Sa Punta de S’Aguila, Sa Terra Rotja and Son Balagueret

facts.text: The hotel is set in a 16th-century finca, or manor house, at the heart of the estate.
facts.excerpt: Sitting at the heart of the estate is the 16th-century Finca - or manor house - which has been lovingly developed into the intimate, luxurious 27-bedroom Son Bunyola Hotel.

facts.text: The original towers of the main house have been turned into two Tower Suites with vineyard and mountain views.
facts.excerpt: The original towers in the main house have been transformed into two Tower Suites, showcasing vineyard views and the mountains beyond.

facts.text: The historic terrace is now home to the pool, and the former olive press has been restored.
facts.excerpt: The former olive press has lovingly been restored, and the historic terrace is now home to the pool.

facts.text: The restoration was done with Mallorcan architects Gras Reynes Architecture Studio and interior designer Rialto Living, using traditional and local materials.
facts.excerpt: Working with Mallorcan architects Gras Reynes Architecture Studio and interior designer Rialto Living, using traditional and local materials was at the heart of the hotel’s design.

facts.text: Some suites have private terraces with sweeping views.
facts.excerpt: to suites with private terraces boasting soaring views

facts.text: Sa Terrassa serves Mediterranean cuisine with sea views.
facts.excerpt: Sa Terrassa, where Mediterranean cuisine is served alongside breathtaking sea views

facts.text: Mallorcan dishes are made from produce grown in the estate's gardens and orchards.
facts.excerpt: savour authentic Mallorcan dishes crafted from fresh produce grown in the estate’s gardens and orchards

facts.text: Guests can swim in the pool and do yoga and tennis, and the landscape suits hiking and cycling.
facts.excerpt: unwind with a dip in the pool, or a spot of yoga and tennis, all while enjoying the awe-inspiring views, but the mountainous landscape is also ideal for hiking and cycling

facts.text: The three villas can be hired year-round.
facts.excerpt: Our three luxury Mallorca villas can be hired year-round

facts.text: Sa Punta de S'Aguila is built into the landscape in traditional Mallorcan style, with panoramic sea and mountain views and a private heated pool.
facts.excerpt: With stunning panoramic sea and mountain views, this beautiful villa built into the landscape in traditional Mallorcan style

facts.text: Son Balagueret villa has a 13th-century turret and a central courtyard.
facts.excerpt: Spread over three floors with a quirky 13th century turret and central courtyard

facts.text: Son Balagueret is available on a self-catering basis.
facts.excerpt: Available on a self-catering basis (all-inclusive on request only).

facts.text: Son Bunyola was awarded a MICHELIN Key by The MICHELIN Guide in 2025 and 2026.
facts.excerpt: Awarded a MICHELIN Key by The MICHELIN Guide 2026 & 2025

facts.text: The terrace looks down over a small village to the bay and the Sa Foradada rock formation.
facts.excerpt: an extensive terrace looking down over a small village to the bay below and the striking Sa Foradada rock formation

facts.text: The spa is small and run by locally based Gaia Natural Products, with a short menu of treatments using island oils.
facts.excerpt: The hotel spa is small but very accomplished, run by locally based Gaia Natural Products with a short menu of treatments using island oils.

facts.text: From the pebble beach below the hotel guests can swim, kayak and picnic.
facts.excerpt: From the empty pebble beach below the hotel (watch out for nudists) you can swim, kayak, and picnic

facts.text: There are not a lot of facilities for children, though there is a smaller pool by the main one.
facts.excerpt: While there aren’t a lot of facilities for children there’s a smaller pool by the main one

facts.text: One bedroom, Room 1, is designed for wheelchair users.
facts.excerpt: One of the bedrooms—Room 1—has been designed for wheelchair users

facts.text: Son Bunyola is a scenic 45-minute drive from Palma.
facts.excerpt: A scenic 45-minute drive from Palma

facts.text: Son Bunyola is around 40 minutes north of Palma.
facts.excerpt: Around 40 minutes north of Palma

facts.text: The estate covers 810 acres.
facts.excerpt: this 810-acre estate

facts.text: The finca is set amid 1,300 acres of olive groves and vineyards.
facts.excerpt: set amid 1,300 acres of olive groves and vineyards

facts.text: Chef Brenda Lisiotti leads the cooking at Sa Terrassa.
facts.excerpt: Chef Brenda Lisiotti brings these vibrant flavours to life at Sa Terrassa

facts.text: Chef Samuel Galdon leads the kitchen.
facts.excerpt: Extremadura-born chef Samuel Galdón worked at the original La Residencia

facts.text: The hotel calls itself Mallorca's most exciting hotel.
facts.excerpt: Mallorca’s most exciting hotel
